summary: Project supported work operations without replay based on their operation ID prefix, and identify guarded claims in bounded diagnostics.

replay.detail: Known work transitions with well-formed operation metadata use existing canonical incremental ordering and affected-tree repair regardless of operation ID prefix. Unsupported kinds, malformed metadata and operation digest/state conflicts retain canonical replay. No startup replay or full-store repair is requested.

schema.detail: No schema, index or migration changes.

rules.detail: No claim vocabulary, admission, operation digest, checkpoint or deletion rule changes.

compatibility.detail: The previous build b3ec817f rejects all work operation metadata; #1710 adds durable cache/ receipts and an allowance for updated receivers. A newer sender can therefore force old receivers to replay each exchange. This follow-up removes the remaining prefix-only restriction for supported work kinds. It cannot change an already-running old binary or support unknown future work kinds. Matching forward fleet upgrades remain necessary; mixed-build validation remains separate.

manual.detail: No setting or canonical-history rewrite. Follow the normal forward rollout; schema17 rollback still requires the documented matching backup.

recovery.detail: Claim-based unsupported/malformed guards emit one bounded JSON detail before replay, naming kind, claim, subject and operation where known. Existing per-Store 16-key plus overflow 60-second limiter and suppression counts apply; identifiers/kind are truncated to256 characters with explicit flags. No new payload query or automatic retry. Original exception text may still quote input fragments; global storage context stays unknown.

downtime.detail: Normal binary restart. Live trigger IDs and replay phase durations were not captured; no production timing or storm-closure claim from focused tests.
